programs.rightsClaimSummary: Acadia's 2023 SEC-filed amended Neuren license describes worldwide exclusive rights to trofinetide for all indications, with royalties, milestones, ongoing diligence and other contractual restrictions; Acadia's current company partnerships page still lists the worldwide exclusive license and August 2026 report confirms commercial DAYBUE sales. Disclosures do not independently adjudicate legal enforceability or absent later changes.

sourceDocuments.assertion: Acadia July 13, 2023 SEC-filed amended and restated Neuren license: worldwide exclusive trofinetide development/commercialization license for all indications; Neuren royalties/milestones and rights obligations.

Current official partnerships page names Neuren and says exclusive global license for trofinetide across Rett and other indications; source is issuer reported, not independent contractual adjudication.
Acadia August 4, 2026 Q2 financial results reports continued DAYBUE commercial sales and markets formulations of trofinetide.
Acadia September 28, 2026 announced USPTO notice of allowance for new trofinetide formulation dosing patent, not proof that license obligations are extinguished.
Phase 3 LAVENDER efficacy and safety trial of trofinetide for Rett syndrome; completed; original basis for historical approval.
40-week open-label trofinetide Rett syndrome extension, completed; not a standalone current FDA filing.
Long-term trofinetide extension for Rett syndrome terminated after March 2023 approval to move patients to marketed product.
Trofinetide 2-5-year-old open-label Rett study terminated following March 2023 marketed approval; Phase 2/3.

trialLinks.indication: Rett syndrome in girls and young women
Rett syndrome long-term safety follow-up with trofinetide
Rett syndrome ages 2-5 years long-term trofinetide safety and tolerability

limitations: Four exact ACAD trial NCTs have current corporate-license disclosure and historic clinical evidence, but these studies are old treatment development/follow-up, with U.S. DAYBUE approved March 2023. Acadia's 2023 SEC-filed license and 2026 partnership/financial updates are issuer claims, not independent legal adjudication or exhaustive contract-chain review. No fresh pending US FDA PDUFA target established for these trials; no Pipeline qualification.
